requirement: Initialization location and timing follow declared collection scope

obligations.note: static var initializer, runs once at first script load, independent of any instance ever being created
member var initializer -- never runs, since no instance is created this run
_static_init() body, fires at load regardless of instance count
_init() body -- never runs, since new() is never called this run
the for-loop header is still evaluated once even for range(0)
runs once per instance -- 3 times this run, but the schema only expresses reached-at-least-once

notes: Each input is its own genuinely fresh process (own `godot --headless --path . --script driver.gd -- <n>` invocation), per the catalog's 'Fresh-process initial state and init events' oracle basis -- not two calls sharing one process's cumulative coverage report, which could never distinguish 'ran once at load' from 'ran once per call' since a real report only ever shows the whole process's cumulative hits. zero_instances gives this fixture real discriminating power at the coverage level: a tool that (incorrectly) treats the member initializer (line 4) or _init() (line 10) as running even with zero instances created would be caught as a false_hit, and a tool that treats the static initializer (line 3) or _static_init() (line 7) as instance-scoped would be caught as a missing_hit in the SAME input where line 4/10 correctly read false. An earlier draft of this oracle used two run() calls within one shared process and asserted contradictory per-call obligations for the same lines -- not evaluable against any real report, since one input must correspond to one measurable run. Corrected before commit. Confirmed on the pinned Godot 4.7.1 engine.

ambiguities: The schema has no obligation kind for 'hit exactly N times' -- three_instances' line 4/10 obligations only assert 'hit at least once', so the exact instance count (3) is verified only via the return value, not via a coverage obligation.
